public_rationale: Companies have reported replacing SaaS functions with custom software, including applications built using Claude Code. Those reports weaken a literal reading that replacement cannot happen. They do not settle the contextual prediction that companies cannot simply replace substantial business software while escaping its operating burdens. No evidence meets the stated early-resolution rule, and the forecast has no deadline.
limitations: The result depends on preserving the contextual meaning of “just.”
Retool sells software for custom development and surveyed customers and builders rather than a representative sample of all companies.
The later deployment report is secondary reporting without a full operational audit.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Companies will not simply use AI to make their own software in place of SaaS.

statement.excerpt: Regardless, my point is that you will not just “make your own software.”

from_speaker: you will not just “make your own software”
Any company of a reasonable size
engineers would have to be hired to maintain it
every single new feature and integration
our_interpretation: Read in context, this predicts that companies will not ordinarily replace paid business software simply by generating their own code with AI. Deployment, maintenance, integrations and responsibility for sensitive data remain part of the claim.
The claim supplies neither a deadline nor an adoption threshold. I do not interpret it as saying that no company will ever replace even one small subscription.
Straightforward replacement means a working replacement in sustained business use, with the relevant operational responsibilities accounted for.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that replacements remain impractical because of the stated operational burdens would support the concern. A finite period without widespread replacement cannot conclusively establish this deadline-free negative forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented, independently corroborated adoption across ordinary companies shows that AI-built replacements routinely displace substantial paid SaaS functions while meeting the relevant operating requirements without exceptional implementation or maintenance burdens.

evidence.locator: Section “Teams are already replacing SaaS with custom-built tools”
evidence.explanation: Retool surveyed 817 customers and builders in late 2025. The results challenge a literal claim that replacement never happens, but do not establish representative adoption, AI's role in every replacement, or sustained operating performance.

evidence.locator: Section “The Math Shifts When Software Costs $1,200 a Year Instead of $40,000,” first paragraph
evidence.explanation: The report describes Greenleaf replacing Salesforce using Replit and Claude Code and leaving additional software vendors. This is material evidence against an absolute impossibility claim, but the secondary reporting does not establish the maintenance, compliance and durability conditions needed for early resolution.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Corroborated records showing routine, sustained AI-built SaaS replacement across ordinary companies, including implementation and maintenance requirements, could contradict the forecast. Continued non-occurrence alone cannot conclusively support a forecast with no deadline.
